newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 6.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Police named the fundamentalist group Abu Sayyaf as the principal suspect in the Tuesday killing of Bishop Benjamin de Jesus, apostolic vicar of Sulu and Tawi-tawi. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER, THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL, TODAY, THE MANILA TIMES)
-Pope John Paul II condemned the "senseless killing" of Jolo Bishop Benjamin de Jesus and called for "divine strength and comfort on all who mourn their Pastor." (MANILA CHRONICLE)
-The Department of Justice recommended the filing of child-abuse charges against an HIV positive patient for exposing her 16-year old boyfriend to the deadly AIDS virus. (TODAY)

- The national inflation rate dropped to five percent in January from 5.2 percent posted in December 1996 despite upward pressure from a series of oil price hikes, the National Statistics Office said. Economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said he expected inflation in 1997 to reach 6.4 percent. (ALL PAPERS)
- Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co posted 1996 net income of 6.44 billion pesos, up 11.98 percent from 5.751 billion pesos the previous year. (ALL PAPERS)
